title: He knew they would fail Him.
paragraphs: He knew they would fail Him.

Because we don’t struggle to serve strangers.
We struggle to serve people who disappoint us.

The ones who ignore us.
The ones who misunderstand us.
The ones who will never say thank you.
Sometimes we already know who will hurt us next.

John 13 tells us that “Jesus knew that the Father had given all things into His hands… and that He had come from God and was going back to God”—and then He got up, took a towel, and washed their feet.
Because we’ve been taught to protect ourselves once we see pain coming.

Pull back.
Close off.
Serve less.
Love carefully.

The hands that formed the stars…
Are now holding dirty feet.

The King of Heaven…
Is kneeling in a room full of future deserters.
The one who would sell Him for silver.
Because this is where it gets uncomfortable.
We love the idea of humility…
Until we’re asked to serve people who don’t deserve it.
Until someone sins against us in a way that feels personal.
Who have you quietly stopped serving because they hurt you?
Who do you avoid loving because you already see the outcome?
Who did you downgrade in your heart… while still pretending everything is okay on the outside?
Because it says, “I will love… as long as it’s safe.”
But Jesus shows us a love that isn’t safe.

Humility is not blindness to betrayal.
It’s obedience in full awareness of it.
Philippians 2:6–8 says though He was in very nature God, He did not grasp His status—but “made Himself nothing… taking the form of a servant… becoming obedient to death—even death on a cross.”
And here’s the mirror you can’t avoid—

We don’t struggle to understand humility.
We struggle to choose it when it hurts.
Because the same Jesus who washed feet…
The towel in John 13 becomes the wood of Calvary.
And the cleansing goes deeper than dirt.
Romans 5:8 says, “While we were still sinners, Christ died for us.”
While we were still walking in betrayal.
You are not just Peter in denial.
You are not just the disciples who ran.
You are also Judas in your moments of choosing other things over Christ.
This is where religion gets exposed.
Because religion says, “Clean yourself first, then come.”
Jesus says, “Come, and I will wash you.”
So what do you do with that kind of love?
Because you cannot receive the cleansing of Jesus…
And still cling to the pride that resists becoming like Him.
You are not called to protect your image.
You are called to reflect Christ.
You are not a victim of people’s failure.
You are a vessel of God’s mercy.
That means loving when it’s inconvenient.
But because Jesus already gave it.
Maybe you’ve been pouring into people who give nothing back.
Maybe you’ve been hurt more than you want to admit.
And part of you is saying, “Enough.”

You don’t serve from their response.
You serve from His cross.
And when you fail—and you will—
Run back to the Savior who still kneels, still washes, still restores.
1 John 1:9 says if we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us and cleanse us from all unrighteousness.
There is no stain too deep.
No pride too strong that His grace cannot break.
But because you’ve already received it.
And if this stirred something in you…
That’s not guilt trying to crush you.
That’s grace trying to wake you up.
You don’t have to stay stuck.
You don’t have to stay guarded.
Jesus didn’t just show you humility.
He made a way for you to live it.
We’re going deeper into the moment Peter resisted the washing—and why some people reject the very grace they desperately need.
